follow-up time: Until neonatal intensive care unit discharge
outcome: Survival to neonatal intensive care unit discharge
cohort: 478 pregnant patients admitted between 22+0/7 and 24+6/7 weeks gestation facing delivery from 2011-2015
finding: When postnatal resuscitation was planned at 22 and 23 weeks gestation, women were more likely to receive antenatal steroids, magnesium sulfate, and antibiotics; provision of this bundle imparted survival benefit at 23 weeks gestation but could not be demonstrated at 22 weeks gestation because of the small sample size.
mod_finding: In singleton pregnancies, the odds of survival to neonatal intensive care unit discharge was not improved by cesarean delivery vs vaginal delivery, even after adjustment for the use of additional interventions, weight, gender, and gestational age.
